body:
You are drafting DIALOGUE LINES for a video game. Reply in plain text only, in the exact format asked. No commentary.

## The game
"The Crooked Moon" is a single-player turn-based tactical party RPG (fully voiced, branching dialogue, skill checks, a storyteller Narrator). Folk-horror campaign set in Druskenvald, an afterlife realm of endless night under a gargantuan crescent moon with a leering crone's face. Drawn like a 1960s monster cartoon stuck in Halloween, but the story is real folk horror: stakes, doomed innocents, sacrifice. Humour is deadpan and sits inside the dread. Everything is our own invention in our own words.

## This chapter: Maidenmist Cemetery
South-east of the village of Wickermoor, an endless fogbound cemetery fenced with cold iron is really a prison built over a tear into the Shroud, the mist of death that rings the realm. Wrathful soul-stripped spirits called the shrouded would pour out of it. Its sexton is YORGRIM, the ghost of an orc seer of the Shadestone Clan, who was tricked by his chieftain into a ritual that annihilated his whole clan's souls; he drags a gravestone carved with their names chained to his back as penance. He is dour, stoic, few words, never cruel, tells what matters, and grows vaguer and more distracted as the chapter goes; deep slow orc bass, short flat sentences, long pauses. His spectral black hound ISOLDE (white eyes, a hooded lantern in her mouth) does not speak: only the Narrator describes her. He asked five friends to kindle balefire beacons from fragments of their souls: Sir Marius Renathyr (knight of a morning god, horse Dawn, King Viktor Denathria), Lethica Nightborne (priestess of the Nightmother, barn owl, loved Marius), Ol' Jericho Sticks (kindly scarecrow banjo man), Captain Briggsy Kratch (pirate with a heart of gold, lucky, a swordsman and schemer), Farryn of the Greenwood (satyr druid of the Green Queen, loved Gwenna). They fell to the Horned King's sin and the heroes (the player's party of four, level nine) killed them. The beacons went dark, the tear grew, the dead walked into Wickermoor. The heroes relight the beacons with Final Rites that honour who the Fallen were before they fell, then go below, where Yorgrim breaks and becomes the Chained Reaper; they destroy him and perform his own rites to seal the tear.
Wickermoor people: MORI SHADE, undertaker, grave, stately, white hair, all black, a fount of folklore, follows the Strangers' ways learned from Yorgrim; DORIS SQUIRE, constable, tall, stocky, says the fewest words possible, flat northern burr; TOBIAS DIBBS, Mori's apprentice, relentlessly cheerful and practical; HESTER BOLTON, annoyed her husband Gregor is now a ghast and still owes rent; ADELA DRUSKENVALD (transatlantic 1920s patter); WESTON MURDOCH (warm revival preacher); Theodora Mayville the postmaster is secretly a pigeon hag.

## The Narrator
The Narrator is the Vagrant, a frog-faced ferryman telling the tale afterwards: warm, folksy, wry, fond of the party; never gloats. Second person, present tense, only what a hero could perceive, concrete senses (smell, sound, texture), no game words (HP, roll, level, check, DC, save), no modern slang, never "suddenly". Never name a specific hero (the party is addressed as "you" or "the party").

## Format rules
- One line of plain text per key, written as `key: text`. No quotes around the text, no stage directions, no asterisks, no emoji, no em dashes (use commas, periods, colons), straight quotes only, no brackets.
- A spoken line is one to three short sentences, 12 to 38 words, never over 45. Narrator lines are one or two sentences, never over 45 words. People speak plainly in their own voice; they do not explain the plot to the audience.
- Obey each brief's sentence count and content. Every line must carry a concrete detail.
- Do not put speaker names at the start of the text. Do not repeat the brief.


## Lines to draft (key | speaker | mood | brief). Reply with one `key: text` line for each key and nothing else.

azure_ask: Speak the last rites over this cold iron lantern, strangers. Lay my spirit down so the ragged tear above us can finally close.
azure_prompt: Overhead the ragged tear shudders in the stone, while the pale flame inside the hooded lantern waits for your words.
azure_hint: Five beacons burn above the grave dirt now, leaving only the old sexton himself to honour.
azure_hint_plain: The right words sit cold on the tip of your tongue, just out of reach in the damp air.
sealed: The hooded lantern blazes white-blue until the whole stone vault washes out in blinding light. When your sight clears, the cracked ceiling is whole, the tomb rests in calm azure glow, and every shrieking shrouded is gone.
sealed_thanks: Thank you, strangers, for lifting the heavy stone from my back before the quiet takes me.
azure_a_intro: You turn the final rite toward the old sexton's tireless care for the dead and the quiet customs he kept.
azure_a_okline: The hooded lantern flares bright against the damp stone as your words land true. Even the cold grave dirt seems to remember the graves he tended and the rites he kept.
azure_a_missline: Your words fall short in the damp vault, and the grey Shroud whispers back a hollow mockery of his graveside rites. Overhead, the ragged tear shudders wide and spills a fresh breath of grave chill.
azure_b_intro: You turn the final rite toward his heavy duty to the Shadestone Clan and the carved names he dragged behind him.
azure_b_okline: The hooded lantern flares with a steady blue heat as your words land true. The iron chains on the cracked headstone ring once, honouring his long duty to the Shadestone Clan.
azure_b_missline: Your words fall short against the stone, and the grey Shroud hisses a mocking echo of the Shadestone Clan's lost names. Overhead, the ragged tear shudders and widens in the vault roof.
azure_c_intro: You turn the final rite toward the five friends who answered his call and the loyal black hound at his heel.
azure_c_okline: The hooded lantern flares warm in Isolde's jaws as your words land true. The pale flame steadies, honouring the five friends he trusted and the spectral hound who never left his side.
azure_c_missline: Your words fall short in the cold dark, and the Shroud whispers a cruel echo of his fallen friends and his white-eyed hound. Overhead, the ragged tear shudders and leaks black mist.
raid_open: The iron clock-tower bells clang late into the Dusk Hour across the slick cobbles. Pale ghasts shriek down Wickermoor's narrow streets, tearing into anyone slow enough to be caught in the fog.
raid_doris: Grave dirt is open and the dead are walking the cobbles. My militia is stretched thin across the lanes, so grab a weapon if you mean to help.
inspect: Some of these corpses have lain under the sod for centuries, and others scarce a fortnight. The freshest rot here is Gregor Bolton, who tumbled off the Mayor's slate roof last month.
inspect_fail: The torn corpses are too far gone to read by lantern light, and the sour stench of grave rot is not helping.
delay: My people will hold the barricades with pitchforks and cold iron, though we will bleed for every yard. I have a long memory for strangers who stand dry under the eaves while neighbours die.
go_fight: Clear the barricade, lads, and give these armed strangers room to work toward the market square.
after_cost: Four of my night watch went down in the mud while we waited on the road. Their lanterns are cold on the cobbles now, and I have widows to wake before dawn.
after_clean: Not one villager was dragged into the fog tonight, and every threshold still has its lock. You have my thanks, strangers, and you will not hear me say it twice.
after_gregor: That fresh corpse by the pump was Gregor Bolton, the roofer who broke his neck off the Mayor's gables. Mori Shade will want word of this before the undertaker's cart makes its rounds.
militia_start: Four posts need holding before the fog thickens, and I have only four volunteers left. We must cover the bell tower, the south bridge, the forge, and the funeral lane. Point them where they belong, quick.
post_bell: The high bell tower needs a sharp lookout who can ring clear signals across the steep slate rooftops.
post_bell_right: Howie works the heavy hemp ropes like a choir conductor, and every dark street hears the iron warning in time.
post_bell_wrong: The bronze bell clangs out of rhythm in the fog, and the stumbled warning reaches the lower lanes too late.
post_bridge: The narrow south bridge needs an archer with a steady eye and a heavy longbow to hold the planks.
post_bridge_right: Hilda looses grey-goose shafts into the mist one by one, dropping every shambling shape before a claw touches the bridge planks.
post_bridge_wrong: The slick timber bridge holds against the clawing press, barely, and the splintering rail will not last long.
post_forge: The roadside forge needs a steady hand at the bellows who can coat iron blades in molten silver fast.
post_forge_right: Jean silvers a full rack of billhooks and knives before the first shriek dies away, giving the militia real teeth.
post_forge_wrong: The coal fire burns sluggish and smoky, and the freshly silvered blades reach the barricades far too late.
